Package org.dellroad.muxable

Interface NestedChannelRequest<I extends SelectableChannel & ReadableByteChannel,O extends SelectableChannel & WritableByteChannel>

Type Parameters:
I - input channel type
O - output channel type
All Known Implementing Classes:
DefaultNestedChannelRequest, SimpleNestedChannelRequest
public interface NestedChannelRequest<I extends SelectableChannel & ReadableByteChannel,O extends SelectableChannel & WritableByteChannel>
Represents a request from one end of a MuxableChannel to the other to create a new nested channel.

Instances provide access to the input and output I/O streams associated with the new nested channel, as well any application-specific byte[] data associated with the request by the initiator.

The input and output function independently, but they are considered part of the same connected nested channel. Unlike TCP sockets, they do not support shutting down only one direction: closing either input or output results in both channels being closed.

See Also:

    • getInput

      I getInput()
      Get the input channel, if any. This corresponds to the output channel on the remote side.

      It's possible that the returned channel requires a non-default SelectorProvider; if so, that must be documented by the implementation. Unless specified otherwise, the default SelectorProvider may be assumed. In any case, the channels returned by getInput() and getOutput() must share the same SelectorProvider.

      Closing this channel also closes the channel returned by getOutput().

      In some implementations, getInput() and getOutput() may return the same channel; this is explicitly permitted.

      Returns:
      the input channel associated with this instance, or null if this instance was created with only an output channel

    • getOutput

      O getOutput()
      Get the output channel, if any. This corresponds to the input channel on the remote side.

      It's possible that the returned channel requires a non-default SelectorProvider; if so, that must be documented by the implementation. Unless specified otherwise, the default SelectorProvider may be assumed. In any case, the channels returned by getInput() and getOutput() must share the same SelectorProvider.

      Closing this channel also closes the channel returned by getInput().

      In some implementations, getInput() and getOutput() may return the same channel; this is explicitly permitted.

      Returns:
      the output channel associated with this instance, or null if this instance was created with only an input channel
